trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Decentralized application requesting DID authentication. Untrusted web context, can request arbitrary permissions. Nonce and path parameters must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Decentralized Application
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web application invoking Provider methods. Runs in untrusted browser context, can invoke arbitrary RPC methods, send malformed requests. All input must be sanitized.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet/Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Ethereum wallet software that processes RPC requests. Assumed to be locally installed and somewhat trusted, but responses should still be validated. User has consented to trust this software.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum blockchain network. Consensus provides authentication of block data but network connectivity and response content must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Human user controlling account access permissions. User actions are authoritative for their own accounts but may be socially engineered. UI should clearly present consequences.

trusted_external_entities.name: Potentially Malicious DApp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled as untrusted/malicious web application. Must assume worst-case behavior: arbitrary data injection, DoS attempts, phishing UI. Full input validation and rate limiting required.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying logs via JSON-RPC interface. Can send arbitrary filter parameters, malformed block hashes. All input parameters must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployment Source
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Compiler or deployment tool submitting EOF bytecode. Bytecode is arbitrary and untrusted. Full structural validation of EOF container required before deployment.

trusted_external_entities.name: Verification Tool
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block explorer or verification service requesting source verification. Request parameters untrusted. Metadata content should not be trusted to accurately represent source.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Another Ethereum node on the P2P network. May be malicious, misconfigured, or compromised. All status messages, block range claims, and data must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Requesting Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer requesting receipt data. Request parameters untrusted, may request arbitrary blocks. Rate limiting and response size controls required.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Nonce must be verified for freshness to prevent replay attacks. Path permissions must be explicitly approved by user.
Request arguments must be validated for proper structure. Method field required. Rate limiting must be enforced.
Wallet is trusted to provide correct RPC results. DApp should still validate response format.
Error codes and messages from wallet are trusted but DApp should handle all error cases gracefully.
Network connection events are trusted but chainId must be validated against expected network.
User consent is authoritative for account access. Wallet UI must clearly present what is being authorized.
User revocation must be honored immediately. DApp must handle account removal gracefully.
All input must be sanitized. Rate limiting enforced. Provider-Wallet isolation must be maintained. No private data in Provider.
Filter parameters must be validated. blockHash mutual exclusivity with fromBlock/toBlock enforced. Block hash format validated.
EOF bytecode is arbitrary and untrusted. Full header and metadata validation required. Invalid containers must be rejected.
Verification requests untrusted. Metadata may not accurately represent source. IPFS content may be unavailable or malicious.
Block range claims must be verified when requesting data. Peers that fail to serve claimed ranges should be penalized.
Request parameters untrusted. Response size must be bounded. Rate limiting recommended.
